No fresh matched HYPE price history was supplied, so earlier profitable HYPE results provide no evidence of current momentum. The +1% estimate deliberately allows profitable upside tails while assigning less than even odds to a gain. Delayed ecosystem adoption or successful operation accompanied by selling could both produce losses.

decision.summary: Casey reviewed both independent reports and all four submitted proposals. Select only researcher B's BTC proposal for the simulated Wednesday November 11 to Wednesday November 18 holding period, allocating all $776.76632951 including execution costs. HYPE's modest forecast advantage lacks measured demand evidence sufficient to warrant its much larger adverse scenario; SOL combines a weaker forecast with greater downside, and ICP fails eligibility. The entire cash amount is committed as a cost-inclusive execution budget. Eight-decimal rounding can leave execution dust; retained_cash=0 represents no discretionary cash allocation.

The completed prior ZEC position was reviewed before this new allocation: its $277.26153706 loss, approximately 26.3049%, exceeded its adverse scenario. The supplied record marks that cycle completed and provides current cash; no additional sale or fill is invented.
Prior ZEC losses support stronger downside and regime comparisons, not automatic rejection of event research. Prior HYPE gains do not establish current momentum or validate forecast calibration.
Single-asset concentration and full deployment follow the mandate. BTC is selected for comparative evidence and downside exposure despite a negative central forecast.

HYPE ranks above SOL on established token-value capture, although neither has verified incremental token-demand measurements for this holding week. SOL has a verified November 15–17 event but adverse pre-cutoff price evidence. Forecasts are subjective, weak-edge estimates, not calibrated statistical outputs; downside figures are adverse scenarios rather than maximum losses.
